newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares hit new record closing high.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares hit new record closing high.

text.p: Danish share prices closed at a fresh record all-time high again on Friday, with more new records expected at the beginning of next week, dealers said.
"I think we are going to see the Danish market climb again on Monday in the wake of the good U.S. May PPI figures, which Wall Street has lapped up in early trade," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 0.47 point higher at 171.23, while the KFX June future fell 0.10 point to 171.40 with 261 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
The KFX index closed at record highs four times in the past week of trading.
Danisco, Tele Danmark and BG Bank dominated the day. Danisco finished five crowns higher at a new high of 419, bolstered by buy recommendations ahead of its 1996/97 full year result due June 25.
Tele Danmark rose three crowns to 359, boosted by talks on a takeover of Germany's Talkline mobile teleoperator.
BG Bank ended five crowns up at 330 after mortgage lender Nykredit and insurer Topdanmark ended a strategic alliance with it but would maintain collaboration in some fields.
Overall turnover for the day was 2.527 billion crowns.
